researchQuestion: With the 6-Space Main Reactor held fixed in footprint, what PF4-1/PF4/PF4+1 output region and what Auxiliary Reactor Space/TP economics preserve tactical scarcity and meaningful ship-design tradeoffs without allowing unrestricted Auxiliary Reactor stacking to collapse the power economy?

stackingPolicy.purpose: Do not assume one-copy-only. Measure whether Space economics alone bound stacking; identify if an explicit count cap is actually required.

combatComparison: Matched legal one-Main-Reactor carrier with N Auxiliary Reactors versus the identical carrier with zero Auxiliary Reactors; remaining Space is mission/noncombat capacity so only installed renewable TP differs in the combat kernel.
mainReactorDamageStateBoundary: Operational output is varied by -1/0/+1. Existing Degraded/Emergency values remain fixed and are reported against the same static/stochastic demand surfaces; full component-damage Reactor state transitions remain a later integration item.
auxiliaryReactorDamageBoundary: This pass calibrates Operational TP/Space and stack safety first. Historical Auxiliary Reactor damage identity is preserved conceptually but degraded/cooldown scaling for candidates above +1 TP is not invented before the viable Operational region is known.
expectedStudyProducts: PF4-1/PF4/PF4+1 Main Reactor support curves at fixed 6 Space
1-4 Space x +1-4 TP Auxiliary Reactor density and Main-Reactor-equivalence tables
exact unrestricted legal stacking envelopes across the full powered architecture population
explicit player-base-cruiser Auxiliary Reactor fit limits by TL
stochastic doctrine allocation response for 1/2/3/MAX legal stacks
matched full-map combat response for Auxiliary Reactor stacks across all 16 Space/TP candidates and all three Main Reactor offsets
stack-risk diagnostics without automatic count caps, tuning, or PF5 promotion
